cards.title: CHamoru as Guam's Indigenous and official language
cards.answer_text: CHamoru—also commonly written Chamorro—is the Indigenous language of the CHamoru people (Taotao Tåno') and is deeply connected with Guåhan and the Mariana Islands. In Guam law, Chamorro and English are the island's two official languages. If someone says it is Guam's ‘native language,’ that is broadly understandable; ‘the Indigenous language of the CHamoru people and an official language of Guam’ is more precise.

cards.title: SYM in a modern Guam school message
cards.answer_text: In a Hurao Academy or similar modern Guam school or institutional message, SYM at the end is used as a compact sign-off for Si Yu'os Ma'åse'—‘thank you.’ Treat this as contextual Guam usage, not a universal expansion of SYM; if the institution or context differs, describe it as the likely reading rather than certain.

What does SYM mean at Hurao Academy?

cards.title: MSY in a modern Hurao or Guam school message
cards.answer_text: In the Hurao Academy context reported to HåfaGPT, MSY is best read as Manana si Yu'os—‘good morning.’ The full phrase and meaning are independently documented by the Kumisión i Fino' CHamoru, while the abbreviated Hurao usage is firsthand user context. Treat this as a contextual interpretation, not a universal expansion of MSY or a claim about formal school policy; if the institution or context differs, describe it as likely rather than certain. Both Manana si Yu'os and Buenas dias are source-backed Guam good-morning greetings; this card explains the Hurao abbreviation rather than declaring one universal form.
